description: Backlog of potentially useful external context sources. Add integrations only after access, licensing, and timestamp safety are clear.

priority.name: Google Trends
priority.notes: Useful as retail/investor attention proxy. Crypto attention is enabled; macro/systemic/market-stress baskets are configured but disabled by default to avoid pytrends rate limiting. Historical exports are rescaled by Google over the requested window, so do not silently backfill old candles with long-window downloads.

priority.name: ETF flow history
examples: Farside Investors Bitcoin ETF flow all-data table
priority.notes: Free HTML table parsed through the global context collector. Daily rows are timestamped conservatively to the next UTC day to avoid intraday lookahead. Keep as institutional context, not media sentiment.

priority.name: Funding rates and open interest
priority.notes: Likely useful with news volume plus local structure. Need source with historical data, clear symbols, and no survivorship/lookahead issues.

priority.name: Liquidations
priority.notes: Useful for shock confirmation. Free long history may be limited.

priority.name: Options skew and implied volatility
priority.notes: Potentially strong for expected move and event risk, but more fragile to source and contract normalization.

priority.name: Social attention/sentiment
priority.notes: Research suggests social/investor attention can be stronger than generic news, especially at extremes. Need careful bot/noise handling.

parked_live_conversation_items.A: Stop treating all hours equally; evaluate event windows separately.
parked_live_conversation_items.B: Add event-trigger filters before modelling: severity, confluence, novelty, source diversity, price structure, and volume expansion.
parked_live_conversation_items.C: Add event-study reports before further broad FreqAI runs: feature spike before/around known events, then post-event return/drawdown/upside.
